costpage.title: Gettysburg College - Tuition & Fees (2026-27 cost of attendance)

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class): 7,928 applied (4,477 men + 3,447 women + 4 unknown), 3,178 admitted (40.1%; 1,635 + 1,540 + 3), 497 enrolled (259 + 236 + 2). The CDS leaves the in-state / out-of-state / international columns of the C1 residency table blank, so no international applicant or admit counts are published there (B2 lists 81 nonresident first-time first-years and 343 nonresident undergraduates). ED: 774 applications, 292 admitted (Fall 2025). SAT scores were submitted by 23% (116 students) and ACT by 5% (23) of enrolled first-years; the CDS leaves the SAT composite row empty and prints '65' for the SAT Math 50th percentile (apparently a typo), so those two cells are left blank. The average high school GPA and the GPA breakdown (C11/C12) are blank in the CDS (all rows 0.00%), so no GPA is shown. Class rank: 42% in the top tenth, 75% in the top quarter, 95% in the top half. Undergraduate enrollment (2,093) and the nonresident count (343) are the B2 'Total Undergraduates' figures; B1 adds up to 1,993 (men 1,009 + women 984), a 100-student difference from B2 (2,086 degree-seeking + 7 other) that the CDS does not explain. Student-to-faculty ratio 9.8:1 (I-2, 1,985 students and 203 faculty, Fall 2025).

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs from the Common Data Set (G1/G5, 2026-27 academic year): tuition $71,730 with required fees $0 (included in tuition), food and housing $17,340, books and supplies $1,000, transportation $1,500 and other expenses $1,200 (other costs shown = transportation + other). The college's Tuition & Fees page (opened 2026-11-03) lists the same 2026-27 items plus $40 loan fees for a total cost of attendance of $92,810; the 2025-26 total there is $89,380 (tuition $68,970). The same page says a College Student Health Insurance plan of $2,856 is required for matriculated international students and students without adequate coverage (the international aid page still prints an older $2,784). Aid to nonresidents (CDS H6, 2025-26 data): 345 degree-seeking undergraduate nonresidents were awarded institutional aid, average $61,565, total $21,240,026; this count is higher than the 343 nonresident undergraduates in B2, which the CDS does not explain.
